decisions.reason: As a close-to-core plugin in a growing firm with hiring and in-house development, it is likely to stay unless early sales clearly fall below aspiration levels.
An ERP interface plugin fits the firm's end-to-end shop integration strategy well and likely offers enough strategic value and customer stickiness to remain on the market.
This tracking plugin is near the firm's core business, but because the firm launched several similar tracking products, management has somewhat more reason to prune it if results disappoint.
The product benefits from strong fit with the firm's optimization offer, though overlap with other tracking plugins raises the chance of later consolidation if performance is only mediocre.
Given available organisational slack and strategic fit, it is likely to be retained for now, but similarity to other tracking plugins makes it more exposed than more distinctive offerings.
A net price reporting plugin is a related extension of the established offer, and in the absence of clear evidence of underperformance the firm is more likely to continue than to withdraw it.
